20번|vocab.blanked: Learning games need to be what we call 'fun enough.' Many new learning-game developers try to design an ①entertaining game. Unfortunately, that often makes learning ②harder rather than easier. Remember, you are not creating the next great commercial game to entertain your learners; you are creating a learning game in which success will be measured by the achievement of learning outcomes. ③Embrace the temptation to create a ton of rules, pile on different game elements, and incorporate multiple dynamics to keep player interest high. Yes, the game should be engaging with a mild level of fun, but learning should be the goal. Focus on engagement rather than entertainment. The goals of the game play should be ④interactivity and engagement. Research shows that what makes games instructional is the level of interactivity and engagement the learners have with the content. Given those parameters, making sure the learners are engaged and active is far more important than making sure they are ⑤entertained.
20번|vocab.explanation: ③이 정답입니다. 앞문장에서 학습 게임 개발자가 재미만 추구하면 학습이 어려워진다고 경고하며, 뒤문장에서 '게임 요소를 쌓고 역동성을 도입하여 플레이어의 관심을 높이는 유혹을 받아들이라'고 주장하는 것은 문맥과 모순됩니다. 학습 목표 달성이 우선이므로 이러한 유혹을 '저항해야(resist)' 한다는 의미로 바꿔야 합니다. 나머지 낱말은 문맥상 적절하게 사용되었습니다.

21번|vocab.blanked: We are ①wonderfully made, yet we don't allow ourselves to participate in the wonder for which we were created. Instead of moving anywhere and everywhere, most of us spend our time moving ②nowhere. We occupy the same square footage of a chair for hours and hours every day. Many kids today are being held ③captive by 'smart' devices like phones and tablets. They are not going outside to play, they are not learning how to socialize and read physical cues from others. As a result they are not learning or building their movement repertoire, the very thing that will help them learn, communicate, create, and become emotionally ④immature. They are not even learning how to run, how to skip, or how to climb. Instead, they are learning how to live with anxiety, depression, and even diseases they were never meant to have. The point is we are getting further and further away from our design. We were made to move ─ and through movement, we are meant to live ⑤extraordinary lives. Movement is life to us.
21번|vocab.explanation: ④가 정답입니다. 앞문장인 'They are not learning or building their movement repertoire'에서 신체 활동과 사회적 기술을 배우지 못한다고 언급하고, 뒤문장에서는 'anxiety, depression, and even diseases'와 같은 부정적인 결과를 강조합니다. 따라서 신체적·정서적 발달이 저해되어 성숙하지 못한 상태임을 나타내는 'immature(미성숙한)'가 문맥상 적절하며, 'mature(성숙한)'는 반대 의미이므로 부적절합니다.

22번|vocab.blanked: Perhaps you have heard of the Law of Attraction, which ①states that 'like attracts like' and that by focusing on positive or negative thoughts, one can bring about positive or negative results. The common ②flaw in our understanding of this law is that we believe all we have to do is think about or visualize something to manifest it. It is true that we attract at the level of our own vibration and that our thoughts and words are extremely ③magnetic. But the most powerful attractor is our belief system. You can create beautiful poster boards full of images of what you want and affirm every day that you are available for an incredibly successful, passionate career or a loving relationship; but if you don't truly believe you are enough, worthy, lovable, and deserving, then attracting a great career or relationship into your life may be more ④challenging. Consider what limiting beliefs you have that contradict your desires and ⑤downgrade them to beliefs that are in line with what you want to attract.
22번|vocab.explanation: ⑤가 정답입니다. 앞문장에서는 원하는 것을 끌어들이기 위해 제한적 신념을 확인하라고 했으며, 뒤이어 'what you want to attract'이라는 표현이 나옵니다. 원하는 것을 끌어들이기 위해서는 제한적 신념을 낮추는 것이 아니라, 원하는 신념과 일치하도록 신념을 '높이거나 강화'해야 하므로, 'downgrade(격하하다, 하향 조정하다)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 따라서 올바른 의미인 'upgrade(격상하다, 상향 조정하다)'로 고쳐져야 합니다.

23번|vocab.blanked: It's important for humans to have many kinds of minds, because ①variation is ②critical for the survival of a species. One of Charles Darwin's greatest insights was that variation is a prerequisite for natural selection to work. Think about it: If there's a huge change in the environment, like a catastrophic drop in the food supply or a big increase in temperature, a species without much variation might be completely wiped out. A species with great variation will more likely have some survivors after any ③catastrophe ─ the members who are well suited for the new environment. Darwin observed variation in the bodies of animals, and the same principle applies to human minds. If we all had the same kind of mind ─ if there were only one human nature ─ then when disaster struck, we might become ④extinct. Thankfully, our species has many kinds of minds, both within a single culture and across cultures, so we're less likely to be wiped out. This variation ⑤threatens the evolvability of our species.
23번|vocab.explanation: ⑤가 정답입니다. 지문은 인간의 다양한 사고방식(variation)이 종의 생존(survival)에 필수적(critical)이며, 자연 선택의 전제 조건이라고 설명합니다. 환경 변화나 재난(catastrophe)이 발생했을 때 다양한 사고방식을 가진 종은 멸종(extinct)될 가능성이 낮다고 긍정적으로 서술하고 있습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장에서 이러한 다양성이 종의 진화 가능성을 "위협한다(threatens)"고 말하는 것은 앞뒤 문맥과 모순됩니다. 다양성은 오히려 진화 가능성을 "보존한다(preserves)"거나 "증진시킨다"는 의미여야 하므로, 문맥상 적절한 낱말로 고쳐야 합니다.

24번|vocab.blanked: Letting go of our need for control, being aware, is a lot about gathering the courage to face ①certainty. Human beings want to know. When we don't know, when things are uncertain, we often feel ②frightened and become inflexible. So we pretend that things are more ③predictable than they really are, even though we actually live with enormous uncertainty all the time. We cling to our plans and ideas about how things should be and turn out ever so desperately. And there's nothing wrong with having plans. I think it's a beautiful thing. But there's a difference between planning and thinking all your plans have to come to ④fruition. American president Eisenhower once said: 'Plans are ⑤worthless, but planning is everything.' Imagine if we all used pencil instead of ink to write in our calendars and planners. Both figuratively and literally. Imagine if we could bear in mind that what we write down, what we think is going to happen, might not be what actually happens. And if we could try our best to be all right with that.
24번|vocab.explanation: ①이 정답입니다. 지문은 불확실한 상황에서 인간이 느끼는 불안과 통제 욕구를 다루고 있습니다. 앞문장인 'Letting go of our need for control, being aware'와 뒤문장인 'when things are uncertain'의 맥락을 고려할 때, 여기서 마주해야 하는 것은 확정된 사실인 certainty가 아니라 불확실성인 uncertainty가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 certainty는 문맥상 적절하지 않은 표현입니다. 나머지 ②frightened, ③predictable, ④fruition, ⑤worthless는 각각 문맥상 자연스러운 의미로 사용되어 적절합니다.

29번|vocab.blanked: To understand how breathing affects athletic performance, we first need to understand how the body makes energy from air and food. There are two options: with oxygen, a process known as ①anaerobic respiration, and without it, which is called anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic energy is generated only with glucose (a simple sugar), and it's quicker and ②easier for our bodies to access. It's a kind of backup system and turbo boost when the body doesn't have enough oxygen. But anaerobic energy is ③inefficient and can be ④toxic, creating too much lactic acid. The sickness, muscle weakness, and sweating you experience after you've pushed it too hard at the gym is the feeling of anaerobic overload. This process explains why the first few minutes of an intense workout are often so ⑤miserable. Our lungs and respiratory system haven't caught up to supply the oxygen our bodies need, and so the body has to use anaerobic respiration. This also explains why, after we're warmed up, exercise feels easier. The body has switched from anaerobic to aerobic respiration.
29번|vocab.explanation: ①이 정답입니다. 지문은 호흡이 운동 수행에 미치는 영향을 설명하며, 산소 유무에 따른 두 가지 에너지 생성 방식을 제시합니다. 앞문장인 'There are two options: with oxygen, a process known as ①anaerobic respiration, and without it, which is called anaerobic respiration'에서 첫 번째 옵션은 'with oxygen'(산소가 있는 상태)라고 명시하고 있습니다. 그러나 ①에는 'anaerobic'(무산소)이 들어 있어 문맥상 모순이 발생합니다. 산소가 관여하는 과정은 'aerobic respiration'(유산소 호흡)이어야 하므로, ①은 'aerobic'으로 고쳐져야 합니다.

30번|vocab.blanked: Keep your paragraphs ①short. Writing is visual ─ it catches the eye before it has a chance to catch the brain. Short paragraphs put air around what you write and make it look ②inviting, whereas a long chunk of type can discourage a reader from even starting to read. Newspaper paragraphs should be only two or three sentences long; newspaper type is set in a narrow width, and the inches quickly add up. You may think such frequent paragraphing will ③damage the development of your point. Obviously The New Yorker is obsessed by this fear ─ a reader can go for miles without relief.
